# Model and source

```{r model}
model_name <- "Lebedeva_2012_ErbB23signaling_qsp"
mod_fun <- readModelDb(model_name)
mod <- rxode2::rxode2(mod_fun)
meta <- mod_fun()
```

* Citation: `r meta$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejps.2011.10.026>
  (open access: <https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3398788/>)
* Supplementary material (Additional Files 1-4: model schemes, ODE system and
  species list; Table S2 of nominal parameter values; GSA supplement; SBML
  file of the model) is linked from the article page.

Lebedeva et al. developed a global sensitivity analysis (GSA) procedure for
signalling-network models and demonstrated it on their kinetic model of
heregulin-beta (HRG) induced ErbB2/ErbB3 signalling in the PE04 ovarian
carcinoma cell line, a modification of the Faratian 2009 model. The model
covers HRG binding to ErbB3, ErbB2/ErbB3 heterodimerisation and
transphosphorylation, the Shc / Grb2-Sos / Ras / Raf / MEK / ERK cascade, PI3K
activation and the PIP2/PIP3 cycle, the PTEN catalytic and phosphorylation
cycles, two-step Akt phosphorylation by PDK1, PP2A as the shared phosphatase of
phospho-MEK and phospho-Akt, inhibition of active Raf by ppAkt, and two-step
binding of the anti-ErbB2 antibody pertuzumab (2C4). The paper's key readout is
the area under the 60-minute time course of phosphorylated Akt, normalised by
its theoretical maximum, in the absence (`S_pAkt`) and presence
(`S_pAktPer`) of pertuzumab.

```{r structure}
data.frame(
  quantity = c("ODE states", "reaction rates", "ini() parameters"),
  n = c(length(mod$state), 56L, length(mod$theta))
) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

The 54 ODE states are the 53 species of the authors' SBML file plus
`auc_pakt`, the running integral of pAkt. The paper reports "54 ODEs and 91
parameters": the 91 are the 89 entries of Supplementary Table S2 plus the two
fixed external concentrations (HRG and pertuzumab), which enter here as doses.

# Population

```{r population}
str(meta$population)
```

The model describes one cell line in culture, not a population of subjects. It
was calibrated to western-blot time courses of pErbB3, pAkt and pErk in PE04
cells stimulated with 1 nM heregulin-beta, with and without 100 nM pertuzumab
(Faratian 2009 data; Additional File 1, Fig. S6). The model is deterministic:
the paper reports no between-cell variability and no residual-error model.

# Source trace

| Model element | Source |
|---|---|
| Species, reactions and rate laws | SBML file (Additional File 4), cross-checked against the system of ODEs S1.1-S1.54 and rate equations V1-V58 of Additional File 1 |
| Species names and abbreviations | Additional File 1, Supplementary Table S1 |
| All 89 nominal parameter values (13 total protein concentrations, 76 kinetic constants) | Supplementary Table S2 (Additional File 2), column 'Nominal parameter value' |
| `k_9`, `k57`, `Kd_57`, `k58`, `Kd_58`, `bpV`, `LY` | SBML file parameters (not in Table S2; inactive because `bpV = LY = 0`) |
| Resting PTEN / pPTEN split | SBML initial concentrations (4.5644 / 25.4356 nM), reproduced in `model()` as the steady state of reactions V35/V36 at total PTEN |
| HRG dose 3000 (model units) | SBML initial concentration of HRG; corresponds to 1 nM HRG in the medium (Methods, Cell culture) |
| Pertuzumab dose 300000 (model units) | 100 nM pertuzumab in the medium (Methods, Cell culture) on the same medium-to-cytoplasm scale as HRG; the curated BioModels entry BIOMD0000000424 of the predecessor model (Faratian 2009) gives Per = 300000 |
| pAkt definition | Methods S.1.4: (pAkt-PIP3 + ppAkt-PIP3 + pAkt-PIP3-PP2A + ppAkt-PIP3-PP2A) / Akt_tot |
| `S_pAkt,n` = integral of pAkt over 0-T divided by T, T = 60 min | Methods S.3.1 |
| Parameter ranges for the GSA (uniform between Min and Max) | Table S2 columns 'Min' / 'Max'; uniform linear sampling per Additional File 3, Fig. S7 |

## Dimensional analysis

Time is in seconds and every concentration in nM. Each rate is in nM/s:

| Rate-law form | Parameter units | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `k * (A * B - Kd * AB)` | `k` 1/(nM*s), `Kd` nM | V1, V2, V5, V7, V27, V31, V32, V39, V45, V49 |
| `k * (A - Ke * B)` | `k` 1/s, `Ke` unitless | V3, V54; V28 with `k_28` |
| `k * A - k_r * B` | both 1/s | V6, V50 |
| `k * A` | 1/s | V17, V18, V21, V22, V30, V33, V34, V42, V43, V46-V48, V51, V53, V55, V56 |
| `V * S / (K + S)` | `V` nM/s, `K` nM | V4, V10, V12, V24, V26, V35, V36, V40, V44 |
| `k * E * S / (K + S)` | `k` 1/s, `K` nM | V11, V13, V15, V19, V23, V25 |
| `k * A * B - Kd * AB` (SBML form) | `k` 1/(nM*s), `Kd` 1/s | V16, V41 (see Assumptions and deviations) |

# Simulation of the calibration experiment

HRG (1 nM in the medium, 3000 in model units) is added at time zero, alone or
together with pertuzumab (100 nM in the medium, 300000 in model units). The
experiments added pertuzumab 15 minutes before HRG; the effect of that
pre-incubation on the model is shown further below.

```{r sim-baseline}
obs_times <- c(seq(0, 120, by = 2), seq(130, 3600, by = 10))
ev_hrg <- et(amt = 3000, cmt = "hrg", time = 0) |>
  et(obs_times, cmt = "akt")
ev_per <- et(amt = 300000, cmt = "per", time = 0) |>
  et(amt = 3000, cmt = "hrg", time = 0) |>
  et(obs_times, cmt = "akt")

sim_hrg <- rxSolve(mod, ev_hrg, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  mutate(condition = "HRG")
sim_per <- rxSolve(mod, ev_per, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  mutate(condition = "HRG + pertuzumab")
sim <- bind_rows(sim_hrg, sim_per)
```

Additional File 1 Fig. S6 shows the calibration: total pErbB3, total pAkt and
total pErk, each normalised to its maximum without pertuzumab. The same
normalisation of the packaged model:

```{r fig-s6, fig.cap = "Model time courses corresponding to Additional File 1 Fig. S6 of Lebedeva 2012 (lines only; the figure's western-blot data are not reproduced). Each readout is normalised to its maximum in the absence of pertuzumab."}
norm <- sim |>
  select(time, condition, tE3P, pAkt, tERKP) |>
  pivot_longer(c(tE3P, pAkt, tERKP), names_to = "readout", values_to = "value") |>
  group_by(readout) |>
  mutate(value = value / max(value[condition == "HRG"])) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(readout = factor(
    readout,
    levels = c("tE3P", "pAkt", "tERKP"),
    labels = c("A: total pErbB3", "B: total pAkt", "C: total pErk")
  ))
ggplot(norm, aes(time / 60, value, colour = condition)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~readout) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("HRG" = "black", "HRG + pertuzumab" = "blue")) +
  labs(x = "Time (min)", y = "Normalised to maximum without pertuzumab", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r s-pakt}
s_pakt <- sim |>
  filter(time == 3600) |>
  transmute(condition, S_pAkt_n = auc_pakt / 3600)
knitr::kable(s_pakt, digits = 4)
stopifnot(
  # Pertuzumab must lower the integrated pAkt signal: the drug sequesters
  # ErbB2 and is the paper's reference inhibitor. A sign error in V49/V50 or
  # a dose in the wrong state would leave the two equal or invert them.
  s_pakt$S_pAkt_n[s_pakt$condition == "HRG + pertuzumab"] <
    0.6 * s_pakt$S_pAkt_n[s_pakt$condition == "HRG"],
  # Methods S.1.5: parameter sets with S_pAkt,n below 0.01 were excluded as
  # implausible, so the nominal set must clear that bar.
  s_pakt$S_pAkt_n[s_pakt$condition == "HRG"] > 0.01
)
```

# Mechanistic checks

## Resting steady state and the PTEN initial split

Before HRG is added every reaction is at rest. The free PTEN / pPTEN split is
computed in `model()` from total PTEN as the steady state of V35/V36; at the
Table S2 values it must reproduce the SBML initial concentrations.

```{r rest}
ev_rest <- et(c(0, 600, 1800, 3600), cmt = "akt")
rest <- rxSolve(mod, ev_rest, returnType = "data.frame", atol = 1e-12, rtol = 1e-12)
state_cols <- setdiff(mod$state, "auc_pakt")
drift <- max(abs(as.matrix(rest[, state_cols]) -
  matrix(unlist(rest[1, state_cols]), nrow(rest), length(state_cols), byrow = TRUE)))
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  quantity = c("PTEN at t = 0 (nM)", "pPTEN at t = 0 (nM)", "max |state drift| over 60 min without HRG (nM)"),
  model = c(rest$pten[1], rest$ptenp[1], drift),
  SBML = c(4.56440422583731, 25.4355957741627, 0)
), digits = 8)
stopifnot(
  abs(rest$pten[1] - 4.56440422583731) < 1e-6,
  abs(rest$ptenp[1] - 25.4355957741627) < 1e-6,
  drift < 1e-6
)
```

## Mass conservation

Each intracellular protein and the phosphoinositol pool is conserved: every
reaction moves material between forms of the same protein. (The receptors and
HRG are not conserved, because V48 degrades the phosphorylated dimer.)

```{r conservation}
ev_cons <- et(amt = 300000, cmt = "per", time = 0) |>
  et(amt = 3000, cmt = "hrg", time = 0) |>
  et(c(0, 10, 60, 300, 1200, 3600), cmt = "akt")
cons <- rxSolve(mod, ev_cons, returnType = "data.frame", atol = 1e-12, rtol = 1e-12) |>
  transmute(
    time,
    Shc = shc + e23hp_shc + e23hp_shcp + e23hp_shgs + shgs + shcp,
    GS = gs + e23hp_shgs + shgs,
    Ras = rasgdp + rasgtp,
    Raf = raf + rafa,
    MEK = mek + mekp + mekpp + mekp_pp2a + mek_pp2a + mekpp_pp2a,
    ERK = erk + erkp + erkpp,
    PP2A = pp2a + mekp_pp2a + mek_pp2a + mekpp_pp2a + akt_pi_p_pp2a +
      akt_pi_pp_pp2a + akt_pip3_pp2a,
    PI3K = pi3k + e23hp_pi3k + e23hp_pi3ka + pi3ka + pi3ka_pi + pi3ka_pip3 + pi3k_ly,
    PI = pi2 + pi3ka_pi + pi3ka_pip3 + pip3 + pten_pip3 + pten_pi + akt_pip3 +
      akt_pi_p + akt_pi_pp + akt_pi_p_pp2a + akt_pi_pp_pp2a + akt_pip3_pp2a,
    Akt = akt + akt_pip3 + akt_pi_p + akt_pi_pp + akt_pi_p_pp2a +
      akt_pi_pp_pp2a + akt_pip3_pp2a,
    PTEN = pten + ptenp + pten_pip3 + pten_pi + pten_bpv
  )
expected <- c(
  Shc = 100, GS = 100, Ras = 120, Raf = 50, MEK = 10, ERK = 10, PP2A = 15,
  PI3K = 200, PI = 300, Akt = 50, PTEN = 30
)
rel_err <- sapply(names(expected), function(p) max(abs(cons[[p]] / expected[[p]] - 1)))
knitr::kable(data.frame(total = names(expected), table_s2 = expected, max_rel_error = rel_err),
  row.names = FALSE, digits = 12
)
stopifnot(max(rel_err) < 1e-6)
```

# Local sensitivity analysis (replicates Figure 6)

The paper's local sensitivity coefficient for parameter `P` is
`C = [S(P + dP) - S(P - dP)] / S(P) / (2 dP / P)` with `dP = 1%` of `P`
(Methods, Local sensitivity analysis), computed for the 89 Table S2 parameters
in the absence and presence of pertuzumab.

```{r lsa-setup}
theta <- mod$theta
log_pars <- grep("^lk", names(theta), value = TRUE)
# The 89 Table S2 parameters; the inhibitor-reaction constants carried from
# the SBML file are not part of the analysis.
gsa_pars <- setdiff(names(theta), c("k_9", "k57", "Kd_57", "k58", "Kd_58", "bpV", "LY"))
# Paper (Table S2 / Fig. 3 / Fig. 6) name of each ini() parameter.
paper_name <- function(x) sub("_tot$", "", sub("^lk", "k", x))

# Set a parameter to a LINEAR value whichever scale it is stored on.
set_linear <- function(df, par, value) {
  if (par %in% log_pars) df[[par]] <- log(value) else df[[par]] <- value
  df
}
linear_value <- function(par) if (par %in% log_pars) exp(theta[[par]]) else theta[[par]]

# S_pAkt,n for every row of a parameter data frame, without or with
# pertuzumab added at time zero.
solve_s <- function(pars, with_per, tol = 1e-10) {
  ev <- et(amt = 3000, cmt = "hrg", time = 0)
  if (with_per) ev <- et(amt = 300000, cmt = "per", time = 0) |> et(amt = 3000, cmt = "hrg", time = 0)
  ev <- et(ev, c(0, 3600), cmt = "akt")
  pars$id <- seq_len(nrow(pars))
  s <- rxSolve(mod, ev,
    params = pars, returnType = "data.frame",
    atol = tol, rtol = tol, maxsteps = 1e6
  )
  if (!"id" %in% names(s)) s$id <- s$sim.id
  s <- s[s$time == 3600, ]
  s$auc_pakt[match(pars$id, s$id)] / 3600
}
```

```{r lsa}
nominal <- as.data.frame(as.list(theta))
perturbed <- function(f) {
  bind_rows(lapply(gsa_pars, function(p) set_linear(nominal, p, linear_value(p) * f)))
}
lsa_pars <- bind_rows(nominal, perturbed(1.01), perturbed(0.99))
lsa_coef <- function(with_per) {
  s <- solve_s(lsa_pars, with_per)
  n <- length(gsa_pars)
  (s[1 + seq_len(n)] - s[1 + n + seq_len(n)]) / s[1] / 0.02
}
lsa <- tibble(
  par = paper_name(gsa_pars),
  noPer = lsa_coef(FALSE),
  Per = lsa_coef(TRUE)
)
```

Figure 6 shows the 39 most sensitive parameters as colour bins 0.5 wide on a
-3 to 3 scale. The maintainers digitised the bin of each cell from the
published colour scale; `fig_upper` is the upper edge of the bin.

```{r fig6-digitised}
fig6 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~par, ~noPer_upper, ~Per_upper,
  "PI", 3.0, 2.0, "k31", 2.0, 1.5, "E3", 1.5, 1.5, "PI3K", 1.5, 1.0,
  "k28", 1.5, 1.0, "Akt", 1.0, 1.5, "k27", 1.0, 1.0, "E2", 0.5, 1.0,
  "V40", 0.5, 1.5, "V35", 0.5, 2.5, "k55", 0.5, 0.5, "Kd_32", 0.5, 1.0,
  "k3", 0.5, 0.5, "K_35", 0.5, 0.5, "k47", 0.5, 0.5, "K4", 0.5, 0.5,
  "MEK", 0.5, 0.5, "k16", 0.5, 0.5, "k_50", 0.0, 0.5, "k50", 0.0, 0.0,
  "Kd_49", 0.0, 1.0, "Kd_5", 0.0, 0.5, "k16_cat", 0.0, 0.0, "k32", 0.0, 0.0,
  "k41", 0.0, 0.0, "Kd_2", 0.0, -0.5, "V4", 0.0, 0.0, "Ke_3", 0.0, 0.0,
  "K35", 0.0, -0.5, "K_d31", 0.0, 0.0, "Kd_39", 0.0, -0.5, "K40", 0.0, -0.5,
  "V_35", 0.0, -2.0, "k42", 0.0, -1.0, "PP2A", 0.0, -1.0, "k33", -0.5, -0.5,
  "k34", -1.0, -0.5, "V30", -1.5, -1.0, "PTEN", -2.0, -1.0
)
bin_dist <- function(x, upper) pmax(0, upper - 0.5 - x, x - upper)
lsa_cmp <- fig6 |>
  left_join(lsa, by = "par") |>
  mutate(
    noPer_bin = sprintf("[%.1f, %.1f]", noPer_upper - 0.5, noPer_upper),
    Per_bin = sprintf("[%.1f, %.1f]", Per_upper - 0.5, Per_upper),
    noPer_dist = bin_dist(noPer, noPer_upper),
    Per_dist = bin_dist(Per, Per_upper)
  )
lsa_cmp |>
  transmute(par, noPer_bin, noPer = round(noPer, 2), Per_bin, Per = round(Per, 2)) |>
  rename(
    "Parameter" = par,
    "Fig. 6 bin, no pertuzumab" = noPer_bin, "Model, no pertuzumab" = noPer,
    "Fig. 6 bin, pertuzumab" = Per_bin, "Model, pertuzumab" = Per
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

```{r lsa-summary}
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  condition = c("no pertuzumab", "pertuzumab"),
  in_published_bin = c(sum(lsa_cmp$noPer_dist == 0), sum(lsa_cmp$Per_dist == 0)),
  within_one_bin = c(sum(lsa_cmp$noPer_dist <= 0.5), sum(lsa_cmp$Per_dist <= 0.5)),
  of = nrow(lsa_cmp)
))
rank_desc <- function(x, nm) match(nm, lsa$par[order(-x)])
stopifnot(
  # Results: "in the absence of pertuzumab, LSA indicated highest
  # sensitivity for the total amount of phosphoinositol (PI) and PTEN".
  rank_desc(lsa$noPer, "PI") == 1,
  rank_desc(-lsa$noPer, "PTEN") == 1,
  # Results: with pertuzumab "LSA predicted the most sensitivity for the
  # parameters of PTEN-phospho-PTEN turnover (V35 and V_35), while the
  # sensitivity to total PTEN and PI3K dropped".
  all(sort(rank_desc(abs(lsa$Per), c("V35", "V_35"))) == c(1, 2)),
  abs(lsa$Per[lsa$par == "PTEN"]) < abs(lsa$noPer[lsa$par == "PTEN"]),
  abs(lsa$Per[lsa$par == "PI3K"]) < abs(lsa$noPer[lsa$par == "PI3K"])
)
```

Every statement the Results make about the local analysis holds for the
packaged model: without pertuzumab the integrated pAkt is most sensitive to
total PI (positive) and total PTEN (negative), with ErbB3 among the key
parameters and high sensitivity to k28, k31, k34 and total PI3K; with
pertuzumab the PTEN phosphorylation cycle (V35, V_35) dominates and the
sensitivity to total PTEN and PI3K drops. The bin-by-bin agreement is weaker
without pertuzumab: Figure 6 shows near-zero coefficients for V40, V35,
V_35, k42, K40, Kd_39 and PP2A, where the packaged model gives coefficients
between -1.3 and 1.3. With pertuzumab, V35, V_35, k42, K40 and Kd_39 fall in
their published bins and V40 sits on its bin edge; PP2A (model -0.3, Figure 6
between -1.5 and -1) and total Akt do not. The global analysis below
reproduces Figure 3 for these parameters. The maintainers verified that the packaged model reproduces
every species trajectory of the authors' SBML file (relative difference below
1e-7), so the gap is not a transcription error. The conditions behind the
published local analysis without pertuzumab could not be identified from the
paper.

# Global sensitivity analysis (replicates Figure 3)

The paper samples 120,000 Sobol points uniformly within the Table S2 bounds
(Additional File 3, Fig. S7 shows uniform, linear-scale marginals), discards
sets with `S_pAkt,n < 0.01`, and computes partial rank correlation
coefficients (PRCC) between each parameter and `S_pAkt,n` or `S_pAktPer,n`. A
reduced version with 3000 pseudo-random points keeps the render time short;
the PRCC standard error at this size is about 0.03.

```{r gsa}
bounds <- tibble::tribble(
  ~par, ~min, ~max,
  "E3_tot", 10, 1000, "E2_tot", 10, 1000, "Shc_tot", 10, 1000,
  "GS_tot", 10, 1000, "RasGDP_tot", 10, 1000, "Raf_tot", 10, 1000,
  "MEK_tot", 1.01, 1000, "PP2A_tot", 1, 1000, "ERK_tot", 1.01, 1000,
  "PI3K_tot", 10, 1000, "PI_tot", 10, 1000, "Akt_tot", 10, 1000,
  "PTEN_tot", 1, 500, "k1", 0.0005, 0.05, "Kd_1", 60, 6000,
  "k2", 1, 100, "Kd_2", 1, 100, "k3", 0.1, 10, "Ke_3", 0.01, 1,
  "V4", 1, 100, "K4", 5, 500, "k5", 0.006, 0.6, "Kd_5", 0.1, 10,
  "k6", 1.2, 120, "k_6", 0.3, 30, "k7", 3.61, 360, "Kd_7", 0.9, 90,
  "k8", 1.2, 120, "Kd_8", 0.01, 1, "k9", 3.5, 350, "V10", 0.00101, 1,

n_gsa <- 3000
set.seed(20120716)
draws <- sapply(seq_len(nrow(bounds)), function(i) runif(n_gsa, bounds$min[i], bounds$max[i]))
colnames(draws) <- bounds$par
gsa_pars_df <- nominal[rep(1, n_gsa), ]
for (p in bounds$par) gsa_pars_df <- set_linear(gsa_pars_df, p, draws[, p])
s_no <- solve_s(gsa_pars_df, FALSE, tol = 1e-8)
s_per <- solve_s(gsa_pars_df, TRUE, tol = 1e-8)
keep <- !is.na(s_no) & !is.na(s_per) & s_no >= 0.01

# PRCC: correlation of the residuals of the rank-transformed parameter and
# output, each regressed on the ranks of all other parameters.
prcc <- function(x, y) {
  rx <- apply(x, 2, rank)
  ry <- rank(y)
  vapply(seq_len(ncol(rx)), function(j) {
    q <- qr(cbind(1, rx[, -j]))
    cor(qr.resid(q, rx[, j]), qr.resid(q, ry))
  }, numeric(1))
}
gsa <- tibble(
  par = paper_name(bounds$par),
  noPer = prcc(draws[keep, ], s_no[keep]),
  Per = prcc(draws[keep, ], s_per[keep])
)
c(sampled = n_gsa, retained = sum(keep))
```

d_no <- gsa_cmp$noPer - gsa_cmp$noPer_pub
d_per <- gsa_cmp$Per - gsa_cmp$Per_pub
strong_no <- abs(gsa_cmp$noPer_pub) >= 0.15
strong_per <- abs(gsa_cmp$Per_pub) >= 0.15

  condition = c("no pertuzumab", "pertuzumab"),
  median_abs_diff = c(median(abs(d_no)), median(abs(d_per))),
  q90_abs_diff = c(quantile(abs(d_no), 0.9), quantile(abs(d_per), 0.9)),
  correlation = c(cor(gsa_cmp$noPer, gsa_cmp$noPer_pub), cor(gsa_cmp$Per, gsa_cmp$Per_pub)),
  strong_with_same_sign = c(

    sprintf("%d of %d", sum(sign(gsa_cmp$Per[strong_per]) == sign(gsa_cmp$Per_pub[strong_per])), sum(strong_per))
  )

top_pos <- function(x, k) gsa$par[order(-x)][seq_len(k)]
stopifnot(
  # Envelope over the 39 published parameters: robust to which parameters
  # land in the tails of a 3000-point sample (PRCC SE about 0.03).
  median(abs(d_no)) < 0.06, median(abs(d_per)) < 0.06,
  quantile(abs(d_no), 0.9) < 0.12, quantile(abs(d_per), 0.9) < 0.12,
  # Every parameter with |PRCC| >= 0.15 in Figure 3 has the same sign here.
  all(sign(gsa_cmp$noPer[strong_no]) == sign(gsa_cmp$noPer_pub[strong_no])),
  all(sign(gsa_cmp$Per[strong_per]) == sign(gsa_cmp$Per_pub[strong_per])),
  # Results: highest positive PRCC without the drug for PI and V40.
  all(c("PI", "V40") %in% top_pos(gsa$noPer, 3)),
  # Results: with pertuzumab, total ErbB2 and ErbB3 carry the highest
  # sensitivity (Figure 3: 0.30 each, up from 0.09). Asserted on magnitude
  # and on the gain over the no-drug PRCC rather than on rank: E2, E3, Kd_49
  # and k_50 lie within a few standard errors of each other, so their order
  # is sampling noise.
  all(gsa$Per[gsa$par %in% c("E2", "E3")] > 0.12),
  all(gsa$Per[gsa$par %in% c("E2", "E3")] - gsa$noPer[gsa$par %in% c("E2", "E3")] > 0.08)
)
```

The reduced global analysis reproduces Figure 3. Without pertuzumab, PI, V40
and PI3K are the strongest positive controls of integrated pAkt, and PTEN,
k42, V_35, V30 and Akt the strongest negative ones. With pertuzumab, total
ErbB2 and ErbB3 and the pertuzumab binding constants (Kd_49 and k_50
positive, k50 negative) gain sensitivity, as the Results describe. The largest
differences from Figure 3 are k28 (model 0.04, Figure 3 0.14) and total PP2A
(model -0.15 and -0.11, Figure 3 -0.26 and -0.20); both keep their sign.

# Code-versus-paper differences and pertuzumab timing

The Assumptions section lists three places where the SBML file and Additional
File 1 differ. None of them changes the integrated pAkt materially at the
nominal parameters. Neither does adding pertuzumab 15 minutes before HRG, as
in the experiments, rather than at the same time:

```{r variants}
s_with <- function(m, ev, tol = 1e-10) {
  s <- rxSolve(m, ev, returnType = "data.frame", atol = tol, rtol = tol)
  s$auc_pakt[s$time == max(s$time)] / 3600
}
ev_no <- et(amt = 3000, cmt = "hrg", time = 0) |> et(3600, cmt = "akt")
ev_yes <- et(amt = 300000, cmt = "per", time = 0) |>
  et(amt = 3000, cmt = "hrg", time = 0) |>
  et(3600, cmt = "akt")
# Pre-incubation: pertuzumab at -900 s, HRG at 0, integral taken from 0.
ev_pre <- et(amt = 300000, cmt = "per", time = 0) |>
  et(amt = 3000, cmt = "hrg", time = 900) |>
  et(c(900, 4500), cmt = "akt")
s_pre <- rxSolve(mod, ev_pre, returnType = "data.frame", atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-10)
s_pre <- diff(s_pre$auc_pakt[s_pre$time %in% c(900, 4500)]) / 3600

mod_sbml_k28 <- mod |> ini(k_28 = 0, k_29 = 0)
mod_paper_eq <- mod |> model({
  v16 <- k16 * mekp * pp2a
  v41 <- k41 * (akt_pi_p * pp2a - Kd_41 * akt_pi_p_pp2a)
  v28 <- k28 * e23hp_pi3k - k_28 * e23hp_pi3ka
})
variants <- tibble(
  variant = c(
    "packaged model",
    "k_28 = k_29 = 0 (SBML file values)",
    "V16, V28, V41 as printed in Additional File 1",
    "pertuzumab added 15 min before HRG"
  ),
  S_pAkt_n = c(s_with(mod, ev_no), s_with(mod_sbml_k28, ev_no), s_with(mod_paper_eq, ev_no), NA),
  S_pAktPer_n = c(s_with(mod, ev_yes), s_with(mod_sbml_k28, ev_yes), s_with(mod_paper_eq, ev_yes), s_pre)
)
knitr::kable(variants, digits = 4)
# Relative change of each rate-law / parameter variant against the packaged
# model, column by column.
rel <- abs(sweep(as.matrix(variants[2:3, 2:3]), 2, unlist(variants[1, 2:3]), "/") - 1)
stopifnot(max(rel) < 0.02)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Source of the structure.** The rate laws follow the authors' SBML file
  (Additional File 4); the equations printed in Additional File 1 were
  checked against it reaction by reaction. They differ in three places, and
  the SBML form is used:
  - V16 (pMEK + PP2A binding): Additional File 1 prints the irreversible
    `k16 * [pMEK] * [PP2A]`; the SBML file has
    `k16 * MEKP * PP2A - Kd_16 * MEKP_PP2A`.
  - V41 (pAkt-PIP3 + PP2A binding): Additional File 1 prints
    `k41 * ([pAkt-PIP3] * [PP2A] - Kd_41 * [pAkt-PIP3-PP2A])`; the SBML file
    has `k41 * Akt_PI_P * PP2A - Kd_41 * Akt_PI_P_PP2A`. In the SBML forms of
    V16 and V41, `Kd_16` and `Kd_41` therefore act as dissociation rate
    constants (1/s), while in V20 and V45 the same parameters are
    dissociation constants (nM).
  - V28 (PI3K activation on the receptor): Additional File 1 prints
    `k28 * [pE23H-PI3K] - k_28 * [pE23H-PI3K*]`; the SBML file has
    `k28 * (E23HP_PI3K - k_28 * E23HP_PI3Ka)`, so `k_28` is unitless.

  At the nominal parameters the three together change `S_pAkt,n` and
  `S_pAktPer,n` by less than 1% (table above).
- **`k_28` and `k_29`.** Supplementary Table S2 gives 0.01 for both; the SBML
  file sets both to 0. The Table S2 values, which are the paper's calibrated
  values, are used. The difference is negligible (table above).
- **`k_9`.** The SBML rate law for V9 carries a reverse term `k_9` set to 0;
  `k_9` is not among the Table S2 parameters, so it is held at 0.
- **Inhibitor reactions V57/V58.** The SBML file carries the PTEN-bpV(pic) and
  PI3K-LY294002 binding reactions of the predecessor model with both inhibitor
  concentrations at 0. They are kept, with `k57`, `Kd_57`, `k58` and `Kd_58`
  from the SBML file, and are inactive unless `bpV` or `LY` is set. The paper
  ran no model simulation with LY294002 or UCN-01 (Figures 4 and 5 are
  experimental), so no model-unit concentration for them is published.
- **HRG and pertuzumab concentrations.** Methods give 1 nM HRG and 100 nM
  pertuzumab in the medium, and state that the GSA held both "at their values
  used in the experiments". The SBML file gives HRG = 3000 in model units, a
  factor of 3000 for referencing medium concentrations to the cytoplasmic
  volume, and sets pertuzumab to 0. Pertuzumab = 300000 applies the same
  factor to 100 nM; the curated BioModels entry of the predecessor model
  (BIOMD0000000424, Faratian 2009) gives the same value for its
  pertuzumab simulations.
- **Pertuzumab timing.** In the experiments pertuzumab was added 15 minutes
  before HRG; the paper does not say whether its simulations did the same.
  Here both are added at time zero, as in the SBML file. A 15-minute
  pre-incubation lowers `S_pAktPer,n` by about 3% (table above).
- **Resting PTEN split.** The SBML file hard-codes free PTEN = 4.5644 nM and
  pPTEN = 25.4356 nM, the steady state of V35/V36 at total PTEN = 30 nM. The
  model computes this split from `PTEN_tot`, `V35`, `K35`, `V_35` and `K_35`,
  so a changed total PTEN (as in the GSA) starts from its own resting state.
- **Fixed versus estimated.** The paper reports the Table S2 values as the
  parameters "identified in one of the best fittings" and does not say which
  were held at literature values during the fit; all 89 are left unfixed.
  The paper reports no uncertainty, between-cell variability or residual error;
  the model is deterministic.
- **Parameter names.** Names follow Table S2 and the labels of Figures 3 and 6.
  Total protein concentrations carry a `_tot` suffix, and `k13` and `k31` are
  stored on the log scale (`lk13`, `lk31`) because those two names coincide
  with the package's canonical PK micro-constants. State names are the
  lower-cased SBML species ids; the SBML pair `E2_Per` / `E2Per` (loose and
  tight pertuzumab-ErbB2 complexes) is renamed `e2_per` / `e2_per_c`.
- **GSA reproduction.** 3000 pseudo-random uniform points stand in for the
  paper's 120,000 Sobol points, and PRCC is computed directly rather than with
  the R package `sensitivity`.
- **Fig. S6 data.** The calibration data (western blots, normalised) are not
  tabulated in the paper; the time-course figure above shows model curves
  only.
- No erratum or correction notice for this article was found (PubMed and
  Europe PMC, checked 2026-11-19).
